'''Peter Novick''' is an American scientist who holds the [[George Palade]] Endowed Chair in the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine at the [[University of California, San Diego]]. His research interests focus on the biology of [[cell membrane]]s, particularly the [[secretory pathway]] and other aspects of [[membrane trafficking]] and [[intracellular transport]].<ref name="ucsd">{{cite web |title=Peter Novick |url=http://biomedsci-db.ucsd.edu/faculty_detail?f=245 |website=UC San Diego |accessdate=16 June 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Novick was born in 1954 and raised in [[New York (state)|New York]]. He received his bachelor's degree in biology from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Novick attended graduate school at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he was among the first graduate students in the laboratory of future [[Nobel Prize]] winner [[Randy Schekman]], and from which he received his PhD in 1981.<ref name="nas">{{cite web |title=Peter Novick |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/peter-j-novick-jfp6kw/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=16 June 2019}}</ref><ref name="trends">{{cite journal |title=An interview with Randy Schekman and Thomas Su ̈dhof |journal=Trends in Cell Biology |date=January 2014 |volume=24 |issue=1 |pages=6–8 |url=https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/pdf/S0962-8924(13)00197-9.pdf|doi=10.1016/j.tcb.2013.11.006 |pmid=24516885 |last1=Schekman |first1=R. |last2=Südhof |first2=T. }}</ref> Novick's work focused on the [[molecular genetics]] of the [[secretory pathway]] in [[yeast]].<ref name="ravindran_2013">{{cite journal |last1=Ravindran |first1=S. |title=Profile of Peter Novick |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=12 December 2013 |volume=111 |issue=1 |pages=3–4 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1321513110|pmid=24335703 |pmc=3890776 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Academic career and honors==
In 1985, Novick began his independent faculty career at [[Yale University]].<ref name=ravindran_2013 /> He moved to UCSD in 2008 as the first holder of the George Palade Endowed Chair.<ref name="ucsdnews">{{cite news |last1=Kain |first1=Debra |title=UC San Diego Names First George Palade Endowed Chair |url=https://ucsdnews.ucsd.edu/archive/newsrel/health/09-08PeterNovick.asp |accessdate=16 June 2019 |work=UC San Diego News |date=24 September 2008}}</ref>

Novick was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2006<ref name="yalenews">{{cite news |last1=Ryu |first1=Jae Hyung |title=Eight profs receive awards |url=https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2006/10/12/eight-profs-receive-awards/ |accessdate=16 June 2019 |work=Yale News |date=12 October 2006}}</ref><ref name="aaas">{{cite web |title=Peter Novick |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/peter-j-novick |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |accessdate=16 June 2019}}</ref> and to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.<ref name=nas /><ref name="nasnews">{{cite news |last1=McDonald |first1=Kim |title=Three UC San Diego Professors Elected to National Academy of Sciences |url=https://ucsdnews.ucsd.edu/pressrelease/three_uc_san_diego_professors_elected_to_national_academy_of_sciences |accessdate=16 June 2019 |work=UCSD News |date=30 April 2013}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Novick is married to fellow scientist and UCSD professor [[Susan Ferro-Novick]].<ref name="farquhar_2012">{{cite journal |last1=Farquhar |first1=Marilyn G. |title=A Man for All Seasons: Reflections on the Life and Legacy of George Palade |journal=Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology |date=10 November 2012 |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=1–28 |doi=10.1146/annurev-cellbio-101011-155813|pmid=22831641 |s2cid=23177212 }}</ref>
